mainTopic: Whether the waving and shaving of a נזיר are essential when he cannot do them, and what happens when a נזיר shaves over an offering that turns out to be פסול
overview: The amud opens by asking whether the waving (תנופה) really holds back a נזיר, as רבי אליעזר holds. A ברייתא says the law of the נזיר applies 'whether he has palms or not.' The גמרא answers with a matching ברייתא about hair and the argument about a bald נזיר. רבינא explains that for בית שמאי a bald נזיר has no remedy, and רבי פדת links this to רבי אליעזר's ruling that a מצורע with no thumb can never become pure. In a second version, רב says the waving holds the נזיר back. There רבי אבינא reads it the other way: for בית הלל the bald נזיר has no fix, and for בית שמאי he does. This reading argues with רבי פדת. A new משנה then teaches that shaving over an offering that turns out to be פסול ruins the shaving, though רבי שמעון says only that one offering fails. The גמרא begins with רב אדא בר אהבה, who learns that for רבי שמעון shaving over voluntary שלמים works, because the פסוק says 'the שלמים' and not 'his שלמים.'

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא suggests waving is not essential
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether missing the waving really holds back the נזיר, since a ברייתא says the law of the נזיר applies whether or not he has palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the waving really hold things back? But a ברייתא teaches: 'This is the law of the נזיר' — whether he has palms or does not have palms!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the waving (תנופה) is essential. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say a נזיר with no palms is treated just like any other נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with no palms cannot do the waving at all. If the ברייתא still treats him as a normal נזיר who can finish, then the waving seems not to be essential. That would contradict the view that it is מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back; is essential (without it, the מצוה is not complete)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
The law of the נזיר (במדבר 6:21)
Palms of the hands, needed for the waving

phrases.english: And does it really hold him back?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the waving, which רבי אליעזר said is essential for the נזיר.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "This is the law of the nazir,"
whether he has palms,
or whether he does not have palms!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (רבי אליעזר's view) that the waving is essential.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that missing the תנופה holds back the נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes a נזיר without palms in the regular law of the נזיר, so the waving he cannot do seems not essential.

steps.title: Counter-parallel: the same wording about hair does not mean shaving is unimportant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by pointing to a matching ברייתא about a נזיר without hair, and shows from the argument about a bald נזיר that shaving can still be essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about the ברייתא: 'This is the law of the נזיר' — whether he has hair or not? Would you also say shaving is not essential? But a ברייתא teaches: a bald נזיר — בית שמאי say he need not pass a razor over his head, and בית הלל say he must pass a razor over his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by bringing a matching ברייתא about hair. It then quotes the argument about a bald נזיר to show that this kind of wording doesn't prove the act is unimportant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'whether he has palms or not' proves waving is not essential, then 'whether he has hair or not' should prove shaving is not essential. But the argument about a bald נזיר, as רבינא explains it in the next step, shows that for בית שמאי a hairless נזיר is stuck. So this wording does not prove the act is unimportant.

keyTerms.meaning: But then (introduces a counter-question that turns the logic around)
So too? Would you really say the same here?
A completely bald נזיר
To pass a razor over the head

phrases.english: But then, that which is taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַנָּזִיר״, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׂעָר,
phrases.english: "This is the law of the nazir," whether he has hair,
or whether he does not have hair —
would you say so too, that it does not hold him back?
phrases.notes: 'It' here is the shaving. The גמרא is asking whether you would really say shaving isn't essential.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: a bald nazir,
Beit Shammai say: he need not
pass a razor over his head,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: צָרִיךְ לְהַעֲבִיר תַּעַר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: he must pass a razor over his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against step 1 by showing its reading of the ברייתא proves too much.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case: the same wording is used about hair, where the act is clearly treated seriously.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'whether he has palms or not' shows the waving is not essential.
steps.terutzMaskana: That phrase only says the person is a נזיר either way; whether the act holds him back is a separate question.

steps.title: רבינא: for בית שמאי, a bald נזיר has no remedy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that 'he need not' in בית שמאי's view really means he has no way to fix his situation, while בית הלל give him a fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבינא said: What does 'he need not' mean for בית שמאי? 'He need not' means he has no remedy. This implies that for בית הלל he does have a remedy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains the words of בית שמאי. This shows that in their view, the shaving holds the bald נזיר back even though he has no hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the bald נזיר cannot shave, and passing a razor over a bare head does not count, so he can never finish his נזירות. For בית הלל, passing the razor counts as his fix (תקנה). Either way, the ברייתא's 'whether he has hair or not' did not mean shaving is unimportant. The same can be said about palms and waving.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the words of בית שמאי
Literally 'he need not'; here it means there is nothing he can do
A remedy; a way to fix his situation and finish

steps.confusionAlert: 'אינו צריך' sounds lenient, as if בית שמאי let him off easy. רבינא says the opposite: it is strict, meaning there is nothing he can do, so he can never complete his נזירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading shows that a phrase like 'whether he has or not' can sit side by side with the act being fully essential. That removes the challenge against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And Ravina said:
What is meant by "he need not" according to Beit Shammai?
"He need not" — he has no remedy.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְבֵית הִלֵּל יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּקָּנָה!
phrases.english: This implies that according to Beit Hillel he does have a remedy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבִינָא: מַאי ״אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ״ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא quoted in step 2 to finish the answer.
steps.raayaObject: That 'whether he has or not' wording does not show the act is unimportant.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבינא's reading of בית שמאי: a bald נזיר has no remedy, so shaving holds him back.

steps.title: רבי פדת: בית שמאי and רבי אליעזר share one principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that this reading matches רבי פדת, who said בית שמאי and רבי אליעזר hold the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches רבי פדת, for רבי פדת said: בית שמאי and רבי אליעזר said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties everything together by quoting רבי פדת. He says בית שמאי and רבי אליעזר follow the same principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both hold that if a person physically cannot do the act the תורה requires, he has no remedy and cannot finish. For בית שמאי the act is shaving the bald head; for רבי אליעזר it is putting the blood and oil on the thumb and big toe of a מצורע who has none. So רבי אליעזר's view is not a strange position; it follows בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what someone said); shows a match with an earlier statement
An אמורא who links בית שמאי with רבי אליעזר
The same thing; one shared principle

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר and בית שמאי, a נזיר who cannot physically do a required act (shaving with no hair, or a מצורע with no thumb) has no remedy. The ברייתא's 'whether he has or not' only means he is still a נזיר, not that the act is unimportant.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Pedat said.
As Rabbi Pedat said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Rabbi Eliezer said the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of step 3 with an earlier אמורא's statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר's view that the waving is essential holds up; he follows the same principle as בית שמאי about the bald נזיר.

steps.title: The source for רבי אליעזר's view: a מצורע with no thumb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies which statement of רבי אליעזר רבי פדת meant: a מצורע missing a thumb or big toe can never become pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which statement of רבי אליעזר? A ברייתא teaches: a מצורע who has no thumb or big toe can never become pure, says רבי אליעזר. רבי שמעון says the כהן puts the blood and oil on the spot where the thumb would be, and that is enough. The חכמים say he puts it on the left thumb, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us which ruling of רבי אליעזר matches בית שמאי's idea, so we can see what the two share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, if the מצורע is missing the body part the ritual needs, there is no other way to do it, so he stays impure forever. This is the same idea as בית שמאי in רבינא's reading: if the ritual can't be done the right way, there is no fix. רבי שמעון and the חכמים both offer a fix.

keyTerms.meaning: Thumb and big toe, where the כהן puts the blood and oil for a מצורע
Purity ever ('never pure' when it says אין לו)
He puts it on its spot, where the missing thumb would be
And he has done his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר and בית שמאי share one idea: if a required part of the ritual can't be done, there is no fix at all.

phrases.english: What is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer?
As it is taught in a baraita:
If he has no thumb or big toe,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a מצורע, who needs blood and oil put on his thumb and big toe (ויקרא 14:14).

phrases.english: he can never become pure.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He puts it on its spot, and he has done his obligation.
And the Sages say:
He puts it on the left one, and he has done his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אליעזר's view, which רבי פדת mentioned in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי אליעזר matches בית שמאי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא that says a מצורע with no thumb or big toe can never become pure.

steps.title: A second version: רב says missing the waving holds back a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version of the discussion, where רב says that missing the תנופה holds back the נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell it another way: רב said, the waving of a נזיר's offering holds him back if it is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the whole discussion again in a second version, opening with רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב says plainly that the תנופה is required. Without it the נזיר cannot finish his נזירות. The next steps ask which תנא this could follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Waving, when the offering is moved back and forth in the נזיר's hands
Holds back; without it the process isn't complete

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is a second way the same discussion was passed down, so the steps that follow look a lot like steps 1–4.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:
Rav said:
Waving for a nazirite holds him back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the whole discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missing the תנופה holds back the נזיר from finishing.

steps.title: Which opinion could רב be following?
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אליעזר, רב's ruling is obvious. Following the רבנן, it seems wrong, since they say even shaving doesn't hold him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is רב following? If רבי אליעזר's, that is obvious, since רבי אליעזר said the נזיר may drink wine only after all the actions. If the רבנן's, there is a problem: the רבנן say even missing the shaving doesn't hold him back, so surely the waving doesn't either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling. Under one opinion it adds nothing, and under the other it seems to go against what that opinion holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר already holds that every action, waving included, is needed before the wine is allowed, so רב would be saying nothing new. The רבנן don't even require shaving, which is the main part of the ritual. So it makes no sense for them to require waving, which is a smaller part.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?
That is obvious, so why say it?
The shaving of the נזיר's hair
Does it even need to be said?

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say according to Rabbi Eliezer,
it is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַחַר מַעֲשִׂים כּוּלָּם!
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Eliezer say: after all the actions!
phrases.notes: He means the נזיר may drink wine only after every step is done, and waving is one of the steps.

phrases.english: Rather, according to the Rabbis:
Now, one can say that about shaving
the Rabbis say it does not hold him back;
is waving even a question?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that missing the תנופה holds back the נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אליעזר it is obvious. Under the רבנן it can't be right, because if shaving isn't needed, the smaller waving shouldn't be needed either.

steps.title: Challenge: the ברייתא about palms says waving is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether waving really doesn't hold him back, since a ברייתא says the נזיר law applies whether or not he has palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really not hold him back? A ברייתא teaches: 'This is the law of the נזיר' means the law applies whether he has palms or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that waving is not needed. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say waving is always needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waving is done in the נזיר's palms. The ברייתא reads the word 'law' as including even a נזיר with no palms, which suggests waving is a required part he can't skip. That supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the law of the נזיר', a פסוק used to teach that the rules apply in every case
Palms of the hands, where the waving is done

phrases.english: And does it really not hold him back?
But isn't it taught: "This is the law of the nazirite":
whether he has palms
or whether he has no palms!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 7 that the רבנן wouldn't require waving.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that, for the רבנן, waving doesn't hold back the נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes even a palmless נזיר under 'the law', which suggests waving is always required.

steps.title: Pushback: the same ברייתא says the same thing about hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the same wording is used about hair. That would mean shaving holds him back, which seems hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about the other ברייתא: 'This is the law of the נזיר' applies whether he has hair or not. Would you also say shaving holds him back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from palms. The same kind of ברייתא is said about hair, and there it can't mean shaving is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'whether he has palms or not' proves waving is essential, then 'whether he has hair or not' should prove shaving is essential. The גמרא takes it as clear that shaving does not hold back a bald נזיר, so the palms ברייתא may not prove anything either.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair
So too? Would you really say the same here?

phrases.english: But then, what about that which is taught:
"This is the law of the nazirite":
whether he has hair
or whether he has no hair;
would you say that here too it holds him back?
phrases.notes: He means the shaving. Would you really say a נזיר with no hair is stuck?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof from the palms ברייתא in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from 'whether he has palms or not' that waving is essential.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same wording about hair would force us to say shaving is essential, which seems wrong.

steps.title: Proof from the bald נזיר: shaving does not seem essential
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a bald נזיר seems to show that he doesn't really have to shave, even according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: about a bald נזיר, בית שמאי say he does not need to pass a razor over his head, and בית הלל say he does need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its pushback: a נזיר with no hair can still finish, so shaving does not hold him back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bald נזיר has nothing to shave. So it seems that even בית הלל's 'he must pass a razor' is only a gesture, and he can still finish without real shaving. That would mean shaving isn't essential, and the hair ברייתא doesn't mean it holds him back.

keyTerms.meaning: A completely bald נזיר
To pass a razor over his head
Needs to, must

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: a bald nazirite —
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַעֲבִיר תַּעַר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: he does not need to pass a razor over his head;
and Beit Hillel say: he needs to!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 9's claim that shaving can't be essential.
steps.raayaObject: That a נזיר with no hair is not held back, so shaving isn't essential.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a bald נזיר and the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: רבי אבינא: בית הלל's 'must' means he has no fix
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא explains that when בית הלל say 'he must', they mean it is required, and if he doesn't do it, he has no fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא said: what does 'he must' mean for בית הלל? He must, and he has no fix.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא answers the proof from the bald נזיר. He reads בית הלל's 'must' as a real requirement that holds him back. The next step finishes his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed בית הלל's 'must' was only a light requirement. רבי אבינא says it is a full requirement: without it the נזיר has no way to finish. So shaving can be essential after all, and the hair ברייתא fits with that.

keyTerms.meaning: And he has no fix, no way to make it right

steps.confusionAlert: In steps 1–4 it was בית שמאי's words that meant 'no fix'. Here, in the second version, רבי אבינא gives that meaning to בית הלל's 'must'. Keep the two versions apart.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avina said:
What does "he needs to" mean for Beit Hillel?
He needs to, and he has no fix,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא: מַאי צָרִיךְ לְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof from the bald נזיר in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל's 'must' was only a light requirement, so a bald נזיר is not held back.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל's 'must' is a full requirement. Without it he has no fix, so shaving can be essential.

steps.title: By בית שמאי there is a fix, against רבי פדת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא's reading means that by בית שמאי the bald נזיר has a fix. The גמרא notes that this argues with רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בית שמאי, he has a fix. And this argues with רבי פדת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אבינא's answer from the last step. It then points out that his reading clashes with how רבי פדת understood these opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that by בית הלל, a נזיר who can't shave the required way has no fix. So by בית שמאי, who don't require it, he does have a fix. רבי פדת had read these opinions the other way, so the two readings argue.

keyTerms.meaning: a fix, a way to fix the situation
it argues with, it disagrees with
an אמורא who understood these opinions differently

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי אבינא: בית הלל say 'he must' and mean there is no fix if he can't. בית שמאי give him a fix. This reading argues with רבי פדת.

phrases.english: According to בית שמאי, he has a fix.
And this argues with רבי פדת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אבינא's answer and notes which אמורא it argues with.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By רבי אבינא, בית שמאי give the bald נזיר a fix, and בית הלל do not. This argues with רבי פדת.

steps.title: Shaving over an offering that turns out to be פסול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a נזיר shaved over an offering that turned out to be פסול, his shaving is פסול and his offerings don't count. This includes a חטאת, עולה or שלמים brought not for its own sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he shaved over an offering and it turned out to be פסול, his shaving is פסול and his offerings don't count for him. If he shaved over a חטאת brought not for its own sake, and afterward brought his other offerings for their own sake, his shaving is פסול and his offerings don't count. The same is true if he shaved over the עולה or the שלמים brought not for their own sake, and afterward brought his other offerings for their own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that if the offering a נזיר shaved over turns out to be פסול, the shaving fails and all his offerings fail too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's shaving is tied to his offerings. So if the offering he shaved over is פסול, the shaving is not a real shaving. Then even the offerings he brought properly afterward don't count for him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only the bad offering fails
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says only the offering that was done wrong fails, and the rest still count. If he shaved over all three and one was כשר, the shaving is כשר and he brings the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: that offering doesn't count for him, but the other offerings do count. And if he shaved over all three, and one of them turned out to be כשר, his shaving is כשר, and he brings the other offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion in the משנה. Then the משנה adds the case where he shaved over all three offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תנא קמא, one bad offering ruins everything. By רבי שמעון, the damage stays with that one offering, and the others still count. If even one of the three was כשר, the shaving stands, but he still has to replace the offerings that failed.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: shaving over voluntary שלמים works for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from the משנה that רבי שמעון holds a נזיר who shaved over voluntary שלמים has done his duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: This shows that רבי שמעון holds that a נזיר who shaved over voluntary שלמים has done his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב אדא בר אהבה draws a conclusion from רבי שמעון's words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים brought not for its own sake doesn't count as the נזיר's required offering, but it is still a כשר voluntary offering. רבי שמעון says that when the נזיר shaved over such שלמים, his other offerings still count (אבל שאר זבחים עלו). That only works if the shaving itself was valid, so רב אדא concludes that shaving over voluntary שלמים is good enough.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'the שלמים', not 'his שלמים'
steps.stepSummary: The reason is the פסוק: it says the hair goes under 'the sacrifice of the שלמים', not 'his שלמים'. So any שלמים is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says: 'And he shall put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the שלמים.' It does not say 'on his שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון holds this. It answers with the exact wording of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'his שלמים', which would mean only his own required offering. Instead it says 'the שלמים' in general. That shows that any שלמים, even a voluntary one, is enough for the shaving.
